title: LATAM launch enablement kit — Dedicated & Private
content:
Purpose:
This is the GTM enablement kit for the LATAM market for Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private launches. The goal is to give Sales, Solutions Engineering, CS, and Marketing a compact set of messages, competitive notes, objection handling, asset checklist, and a handful of ready-to-send drafts for email and press.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
LATAM customers are rapidly adopting LLM features but face two consistent constraints: data residency & compliance, and predictable inference economics at scale. Redwood offers a single runtime that maps to all three deployment models — Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private/VPC — making it easy for engineering teams to start on Hosted and quickly graduate to Dedicated or Private with the same API and operational surface. For LATAM we emphasize local region support, Spanish/Portuguese language assistance, legal/compliance packaging, and partner-led private deployments.

Primary audiences:
- Product engineering leads at fast-growing SaaS companies (Brazil, Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Argentina)
- Platform/infra teams at mid-market & enterprise (banks, telcos, marketplaces)
- Systems integrators and cloud partners (AWS, GCP resellers, local MSPs)

Topline positioning pillars (short bullets for reps):
- Production-first inference: predictable latency, SLA-backed Dedicated pools, and graceful fallbacks to Hosted so apps never go down.
- Control + compliance: deploy in-region or on-premise with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs.
- Cost predictability: reserved capacity and Optimize toolkit to reduce per-token spend via batching, caching, and quantization guidance.
- Developer velocity: same API/SDK across modes, fast rollouts and model versioning, and pre-built examples in Spanish/Portuguese.

Regional competitor notes (quick scan):
- Global hyperscalers (AWS/GCP/Azure managed endpoints): strong local infra but customers complain about opaque cost per token and slower release cadence for new ops features. Hyperscalers win on ecosystem integrations; Redwood wins on developer ergonomics for inference and cost transparency.
- Large LLM API providers (OpenAI, Anthropic): excellent models and strong dev experience for hosted, but limited options for Dedicated/reserved capacity and private on-prem installs — a blocker for financial and regulated customers.
- Local cloud/MSP integrators: can do on-prem and regionally compliant installs but often lack inference-optimized runtimes and the developer-facing API abstractions (rollouts, KV caching, quantization profiles) — opportunity for Redwood partnerships.

Differentiated proof points to use in conversations:
- SLA-backed Dedicated with configurable autoscaling and burst capacity (customers can predict throughput at commit).
- Benchmarks: sample 2x latency improvement for long-context generation vs baseline hosted endpoints on equivalent hardware (internal bench summary attached as asset).
- Cost examples: customer A (marketplace) moved to Dedicated and reduced per-1k-token cost by ~37% using batching + prefix cache in 3 weeks.

Sales FAQ / Objection handling (short Q/A):
Q: "Why not just use the cloud provider managed endpoints?"
A: Managed endpoints cover model hosting but not production inference economics — Redwood offers batching/caching, model variant routing, and quantization recommendations that measurably reduce unit cost without sacrificing quality.

Q: "Can we keep data in-country?"
A: Yes — Redwood Private supports in-region deployments and the Dedicated offering lets customers choose region-resident pools; we also provide integration patterns for KMS/HSM and audit log export for compliance teams.

Q: "We need Spanish/Portuguese support for onboarding and runbooks."
A: Regional success package includes localized onboarding documents and a dedicated LATAM solutions engineering contact for initial deployments.

Ready-to-send assets (short list):
- Customer announcement email (editable)
- One-page sell sheet (localization pending)
- Demo script for Solutions Engineers (long-run, burst, fallback demo)
- Battlecard (competitors + quick counters)
- Template contract addendum for data residency requirements

Draft: Customer announcement email (subject + body)
Subject: Redwood now available with Dedicated & Private deployments for LATAM teams
Body (short): Hola — Redwood Inference now supports Dedicated and Private deployment options optimized for LATAM customers. Run the same API in-region, keep data on-prem or in your VPC, and get predictable latency with SLA-backed capacity. Reply to this email to schedule a 20-minute technical walkthrough with our LATAM solutions engineering lead.

Draft: Internal all-hands announcement (for Redwood teams)
Title: LATAM — Dedicated & Private launch (regional enablement)
Body (short): We are kicking off the LATAM launch this quarter. Key asks: Sales — prioritize customers flagged in the LATAM motion; SE — review demo script and schedule training; Marketing — localize one-pager and social assets. See linked Confluence for detailed timeline.

Customer-facing blog blurb (one paragraph):
Redwood Inference is expanding regional availability with Dedicated and Private deployments for LATAM customers. Whether you need low-latency inference in-region, strict data residency, or predictable unit economics, Redwood’s unified runtime and operations tooling make it fast to deploy and simple to manage. Contact us to try a region-resident demo with your workloads.

Internal enablement checklist (action items with owners) — copy this into a tracker:
- Localized one-pager (Marketing) — owner: Maya Patel — due: 2026-03-17
- SE training session (Solutions Eng) — owner: Diego Alvarez — due: 2026-03-19
- Sales list + outreach cadence (GTM) — owner: Isabella Martinez — due: 2026-03-15
- Partner outreach (Channels) — owner: Arjun Rao — due: 2026-03-22
- Legal contracting templates (Legal) — owner: Lucia Gomez — due: 2026-03-18

Launch timeline (high level):
- Week 0 (now): finalize messaging, localize assets, SE dry run.
- Week 1: soft outreach to 10 pilot accounts, partner briefings.
- Week 2: broader email/PR + partner co-marketing.
- Week 4: collect first-customer metrics and adjust messaging.

KPIs to track (regional):
- SQLs from LATAM weekly
- Pilot deployments started (Dedicated/Private)
- Avg. time from first call to POC spin-up
- Per-token cost delta (pilot vs baseline)

Assets & links to prepare (placeholders):
- Demo repo: github.com/redwood/demos/latam-dedicated (SEs: clone and run)
- Localized copy: marketing/latam/one-pager (es/pt)
- Contract addendum: legal/templates/latam-data-residency

Open questions / decisions needed (notes to PM/Product):
- Which LATAM regions will have official support guarantees (initial ask: São Paulo, Santiago, Mexico City)? Need confirmation from infra on region readiness.
- Pricing nuance: Reserved capacity commitments for LATAM pilot customers — do we allow flexible commit terms in pilot?
- Localization: which onboarding runbooks must be translated vs. simply annotated in Spanish/Portuguese?

Next steps (this doc owner):
1) Finalize the one-pager and place in the marketing folder.
2) Schedule SE dry-run demo and record a 20-minute walkthrough.
3) Send soft outreach to pilot list and capture feedback after first demo.

Notes to self / informal scraps (keep in doc):
- Consider partner-led installations for banks — local MSPs can own hardware while Redwood provides runtime license + remote support.
- Potential case study candidate: marketplace in Brazil that already uses our Hosted API heavily — reach out to CS to propose Dedicated pilot.

Attachments / appendices (placeholders):
- Internal benchmark summary (attached)
- Draft one-pager (WIP)
- Demo script (WIP)

If you’re reviewing this doc: leave comments inline, tag @Isabella for approvals, and add any local/regulatory nuance we missed.
